x-bayeux-tapestry-embroiderers

The Bayeux Tapestry was stitched in the 1070s, probably in England and perhaps ordered by Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother. Its embroiderers are not known by name, though they were most likely skilled English needlewomen. It is about 70 meters long and now hangs in Bayeux, France.
x-charles-alfred-stothard

Charles Alfred Stothard was an English artist and antiquarian born in London in 1786. He made careful drawings of medieval tombs and of the Bayeux Tapestry, which he copied in the 1810s for the Society of Antiquaries. He died in 1821 after falling from a ladder while sketching a stained-glass window in a church in Devon.

George Jones was an English painter born in London in 1786. He served in the army and then painted battle scenes and historical subjects, becoming a member and later the Keeper of the Royal Academy. He died in London in 1869.

Gustave Doré was a French artist born in Strasbourg in 1832. He became the most famous book illustrator of his time, drawing scenes for the Bible, Dante's Inferno, Don Quixote and fairy tales. He lived in Paris and died there in 1883.

Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury was a French painter born in Cologne in 1797. He worked in Paris, painted scenes from history and the Reformation, and served as director of the French Academy in Rome. He died in Paris in 1890.

Philip James de Loutherbourg was an artist born in Strasbourg in 1740. He moved to London in 1771, where he designed spectacular theater scenery for the actor David Garrick and painted dramatic landscapes, battles and industrial scenes. He lived in Hammersmith and died in Chiswick in 1812.

Loyset Liédet was a manuscript painter born in Hesdin around 1420. He worked for the Dukes of Burgundy in Bruges, painting large histories and chronicles in miniature for their libraries. He died in Bruges in 1479.

Jean Colombe was a French manuscript painter born in Bourges around 1430. He worked for the Duke of Savoy and finished the famous Très Riches Heures, and he painted beautiful illustrated histories for noble patrons. He lived in Bourges and died there around 1493.

Matthew Paris was an English monk and chronicler born around 1200. He lived at the abbey of St Albans, where he wrote and illustrated long histories of England and the world, with lively drawings of battles and kings. He died at St Albans in 1259.

Jacopo Tintoretto was an Italian painter born in Venice in 1519. He lived in Venice all his life and painted huge, fast, dramatic canvases for churches and palaces, including the Doge's Palace. He died in Venice in 1594.

Émile Signol was a French painter born in Paris in 1804. He won the Prix de Rome in 1830 and painted large religious and historical pictures, including some for the palace of Versailles. He died in Enghien-les-Bains in 1892.
x-giovanni-villani-nuova-cronica

The Nuova Cronica was written by Giovanni Villani, a Florentine merchant and historian born around 1276, who died in the Black Death in Florence in 1348. The surviving manuscripts of his chronicle were illustrated by artists whose names are not known.
x-peter-of-eboli

Peter of Eboli was an Italian poet who lived in the south of Italy and Sicily around 1196. He wrote a long poem about the emperor Henry VI and illustrated it with lively colored drawings, including scenes of the capture and ransom of Richard the Lionheart.

Eugène Lenepveu was a French painter born in Angers in 1819. He won the Prix de Rome, directed the French Academy in Rome for several years, and painted a famous series of scenes from the life of Joan of Arc in the Panthéon in Paris. He died in Paris in 1898.

Jean-Jacques Scherrer was a French painter born in Lutterbach in Alsace in 1855. He worked in Paris, painting historical and patriotic pictures, especially of Joan of Arc, at a time when she was a national symbol after the war of 1870. He died in Paris in 1916.

Eugène Romain Thirion was a French painter born in Paris in 1839. He painted religious and historical scenes and portraits, and is best known for his poetic picture of Joan of Arc. He lived in Paris and died there in 1910.

Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel was a French artist born in Orléans in 1850. He became famous as an illustrator of children's books, including a beautiful book about Joan of Arc in 1896, and also painted portraits in Paris, where he died in 1913.
x-anonymous-illuminator-vigiles-de-charles
This miniature was painted by an unknown artist who illustrated the Vigiles du roi Charles VII, a French poem by Martial d'Auvergne about the reign of King Charles VII, in about 1484.

John Gilbert was an English painter and illustrator born in Blackheath in 1817. He became famous for drawings of Shakespeare's plays and for lively paintings of knights and battles, and he served as president of the Royal Watercolour Society. He died in London in 1897.
x-anonymous-illuminator-st-albans-chronicle

This picture of the Battle of Agincourt comes from the St Albans Chronicle, an English history written by the monk Thomas Walsingham. The illustrator is not known, but the manuscript was made soon after the events it shows, in the early 1420s.

Julian Russell Story was an American painter born in Walton-on-Thames, England, in 1857. He was the son of the sculptor William Wetmore Story, studied in Paris, and later lived in Philadelphia, where he died in 1919.

Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Flemish painter born near Breda in about 1525. He lived in Antwerp and Brussels and became famous for crowded paintings of village life, proverbs and landscapes. He died in Brussels in 1569.

Josse Lieferinxe was a painter from the town of Enghien in what is now Belgium who worked in Marseille in southern France between about 1493 and 1508. He painted scenes of the life of Saint Sebastian, who was prayed to during the plague, and little else is known of his life.

Michael Wolgemut was a German painter and printmaker born in Nuremberg in 1434. He ran a large workshop that illustrated the famous Nuremberg Chronicle in 1493, and the young Albrecht Dürer was his apprentice. He worked in Nuremberg and died there in 1519.

Hans Holbein the Younger was a German painter born in Augsburg in about 1497. He worked in Basel and then in London, where he became court painter to King Henry VIII and painted portraits that made the Tudors famous. He died in London in 1543, probably of the plague.

Paul Fürst was a German engraver and publisher born in Nuremberg in 1608. He made popular prints, including the famous image of a plague doctor in a beaked mask, and lived in Nuremberg until he died in 1666.

Bernt Notke was a German painter and sculptor born in the Baltic region around 1440. He worked in Lübeck, Tallinn and Stockholm, and made big works for churches, including the Danse Macabre in Tallinn. He died in Lübeck in 1509.
x-john-of-kastav

John of Kastav, in Croatian Ivan iz Kastva, was a painter from the town of Kastav in what is now Croatia, active in the late 1400s. In 1490 he painted the Dance of Death wall painting in the church of Hrastovlje in Slovenia, and very little else is known of his life.

Jean Le Tavernier was a painter and manuscript illuminator from Oudenaarde in Flanders, active between about 1434 and 1462. He worked in Brussels for the dukes of Burgundy, especially Philip the Good, painting richly detailed pictures in their chronicles and prayer books.

Gentile Bellini was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1429, the older brother of the painter Giovanni Bellini. He worked for the government of Venice and in 1479 was sent to Constantinople to paint the sultan Mehmed II. He returned to Venice and died there in 1507.

Fausto Zonaro was an Italian painter born in Masi, near Padua, in 1854. He moved to Constantinople in 1891 and became court painter to the Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II, painting scenes of the city and its history. He returned to Italy and died in Sanremo in 1929.

Panagiotis Zographos was a Greek painter from the Peloponnese who lived in the 1800s. He painted a famous series of scenes of the Greek War of Independence in a bright folk style, after the memories of the general Makriyannis, who hired him in the 1830s.
Philippe de Mazerolles was an illuminator who worked in Bruges in the 1400s, painting books for Burgundian nobles. He was admired for his lively pictures in chronicles and books of hours.
x-byzantine-mosaicists

The mosaics of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople were made by Byzantine artists whose names are not known. They placed thousands of tiny pieces of colored glass and gold in the plaster, creating images that glitter in candlelight, over several centuries.

John Frederick Lewis was an English painter born in London in 1805. He traveled to Spain and the Middle East, lived in Cairo from 1841 to 1851, and became famous for detailed scenes of Eastern life. He died in Walton-on-Thames in 1876.
x-leonardo-da-vinci

Leonardo da Vinci was born in the village of Vinci, near Florence, in 1452. He painted the Mona Lisa and the Last Supper, but he was also a scientist, engineer and inventor who filled notebooks with ideas for flying machines and anatomy. He worked in Florence, Milan, Rome and France, where he died in 1519.

Michelangelo was born in Caprese, Italy, in 1475 and worked in Florence and Rome. He was a sculptor, painter and architect who made the statue of David and painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. He died in Rome in 1564, almost 89 years old.

Sandro Botticelli was an Italian painter born in Florence in 1445. He worked for the Medici family and painted graceful, flowing pictures such as The Birth of Venus and Primavera. He lived in Florence all his life and died there in 1510.

Santi di Tito was an Italian painter born in Sansepolcro in 1536 who lived in Florence. He painted clear, natural religious scenes and portraits, including the best-known portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli. He died in Florence in 1603.

Jacopo Pontormo was an Italian painter born in the village of Pontorme near Empoli in 1494. He worked in Florence for the Medici and became a leading Mannerist, known for his elegant, twisting figures and bright, unusual colors. He died in Florence in 1557.

Fra Bartolomeo was an Italian painter born in Prato in 1472 who lived in Florence. He became a Dominican friar after the death of his friend and hero Savonarola, and painted calm, majestic altarpieces. He died in Florence in 1517.
x-florentine-painter
This picture was painted by an unknown Florentine artist, shortly after the events it shows, in the 1490s. Many Florentine workshops made pictures for sale, and artists did not always sign them.

Antonio Cotti was an Italian painter born in Craveggia, in northern Italy, in 1840. He painted historical and literary scenes in a polished style, including a famous picture of the poet Dante in Verona. He died in 1929.

Benet Mercadé was a Spanish painter born in La Bisbal d'Empordà in Catalonia in 1821. He worked in Rome, where he joined the Nazarene group of painters, and later in Barcelona, where he became a respected teacher. He died in Barcelona in 1897.
x-anonymous-kurz-allison

Kurz and Allison was an American printing firm in Chicago that made colorful lithographs of famous battles and historical scenes in the 1880s and 1890s. Their prints brought the Civil War and the American West into many homes.

Alejo Fernández was a Spanish painter born in Córdoba around 1470 who worked mostly in Seville. He painted altarpieces in a style that mixed Gothic and Renaissance, including a famous picture of the Virgin of the Navigators. He died in Seville in 1545.

Kanō Naizen was a Japanese painter born in 1570 who belonged to the Kanō school, the main painting school of the Japanese military rulers. He lived in Kyoto and is known for his colorful folding screens of the Portuguese traders who arrived in Japan. He died in Kyoto in 1616.

Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger was a painter born in Bruges in 1561 who moved to England as a child. He became one of the leading portrait painters of the court of Queen Elizabeth I, painting rich clothes and jewels in fine detail. He lived in London and died there in 1636.

Robert Walter Weir was an American painter born in New Rochelle, New York, in 1803. He taught drawing for more than forty years at the military academy at West Point and painted the Embarkation of the Pilgrims in the US Capitol. He died in New York City in 1889.

Stradanus, whose Flemish name was Jan van der Straet, was a painter and designer born in Bruges in 1523. He moved to Florence, where he designed tapestries for the Medici and many prints, including a famous series on the discovery of America. He died in Florence in 1605.

Sebastiano del Piombo was an Italian painter born in Venice around 1485. He moved to Rome and became a friend of Michelangelo, painting powerful portraits that mixed Venetian color with Roman grandeur. He died in Rome in 1547.

José Salomé Pina was a Mexican painter born in Mexico City in 1830. He studied at the Academy of San Carlos, where he later taught, and painted historical and portrait scenes. He died in Tacubaya, near Mexico City, in 1909.
